title: Verifications
description: Things waiting to be verified (docs/verifications.md): GET and POST /v1/verifications, GET and DELETE /v1/verifications/{id}, POST /v1/verifications/{id}/notes, POST /v1/verifications/{id}/criteria/{index}, POST /v1/verifications/{id}/close; and POST /v1/orchestrator/tasks/{task}/verification-note, a scheduled task writing its readout with its own task secret. Read and written with a paired device that may send, or this machine's orchestrator token. Refusals are the flat `{error, message}`.

VerificationStatus.description: `open` until the person settles it; `accepted` or `rejected` after, with the reason.

VerificationAuthorKind.description: `person` is a paired device; `session` is this machine's orchestrator token (an assistant through the CLI) or a scheduled task's secret.

VerificationSourceKind.description: Where a record's evidence is read from. `compaction_compare` is GET /v1/usage/compare-compaction over `since`. Any other kind is refused by name as `unknown_source`.

VerificationCriterion.description: One sentence the check is judged by. `index` is its position, from 0; `updated_at` is when it was last marked, 0 if never.

VerificationNote.description: One note. `author` is the session's name when it gave one (a scheduled task writes `task:<id>`), empty for the person.

VerificationSource.description: A data source and its parameters. For `compaction_compare`, `since` is `<n>d`, `<n>h` or a Unix time, 14d when absent.

Verification.description: One record. Times are Unix seconds. `source` is absent when it has none; `schedule_id` is empty when no schedule is linked. `closed_at` is 0 and `close_reason` empty while it is open. `seed` names the record the daemon planted itself, empty for one somebody made.

VerificationList.description: GET /v1/verifications: every record, open ones first by due time, then the closed ones. `at` is the daemon's clock, for a countdown.

VerificationData.description: A record's data source, read when it was asked for. `compaction_compare` carries the comparison; `error` says why it could not be read, and then the answer is absent.

VerificationDetail.description: GET /v1/verifications/{id}, and the answer to every write on one record: the record, and its data source read live (absent when it has none, and on a write's answer).

VerificationCreate.description: POST /v1/verifications. `started_at` is now when absent; `due_at` is required and not before it. At most 12 criteria.

VerificationNoteCreate.description: POST /v1/verifications/{id}/notes. `session` names the writing session when the orchestrator token writes; a paired device writes as the person and may not name one. An Idempotency-Key makes a repeat answer the first note.

VerificationClose.description: POST /v1/verifications/{id}/close: `accepted` or `rejected`, with the reason. Closing it again the same way is answered as done.

VerificationTaskNote.description: POST /v1/orchestrator/tasks/{task}/verification-note with the task's own X-Clawdline-Task-Secret: a task a schedule started writes a note on a record linked to that schedule, as the session `task:<id>`. Answered with the note.

VerificationNoteResult.description: The answer to a note written with a task secret.
